category_title: Year 11 pupils who are demotivated by public reprimands and prioritize task-based feedback over behavioral rewards
student_description: This Year 11 student is highly sensitive to public criticism and punitive sanctions, which cause them to switch off and disengage. However, they are strongly motivated by academic success and respond exceptionally well to task-based feedback (even negative feedback like low marks) and private corrections. They uniquely require a focus on academic goals and private communication rather than public behavioral management or token rewards.

criteria.rationale: Public admonishment causes this student to switch off and dislike the teacher, whereas private warnings maintain engagement.
criteria.check: The tutor delivers any behavioral corrections or warnings privately or discreetly, explicitly avoiding public call-outs or whole-class reprimands.

criteria.rationale: The student perceives behavioral criticism as personal but is highly motivated by direct, even negative, feedback on their academic work.
criteria.check: The tutor frames their feedback around the student's task performance and academic outcomes rather than critiquing their character or general behavior.

criteria.rationale: Punitive measures like missing break severely damage the teacher-student relationship and prompt unproductive responses.
criteria.check: The tutor avoids threatening or applying arbitrary punitive sanctions (e.g., missing break) in response to off-task behavior.
